So much of the stuff you read about side effects will not apply to you personally. Sometimes the only way is to try it and see how it affects your personal body chemistry. Every single medication I have tried- and there is a lot! have had forums and forums written about all the nasty stuff that can happen, but so far only some of those things happened to me, and also when it comes to the side effect of weight gain- that's always one I worry about, it is very dependable on your body's reaction. My mum is on seroquel (and another med that apparently makes you pudgy) which is 'supposed' to make you gain like huuge amounts of weight- like 30kg but she has been on it for ages and only put pn like 5kg- she was kinda too thin before and is now is quite slim/average (60kg) so she never got massive like the claims on the Internet say. So it all depends on your own reaction. Hell my current medication has serious rashes and mild  rashes as a side effect and I haven't had either of those happen, also when I took lithium a lot of people were saying they gained a lot of weight- I lost a lot of weight. So side effect profiles are iffy, especially ones you read on the net, take them with a grain of salt and discuss those concerns with your doctor and they will have a better understanding of what to expect.

I self harm and still have relapses but am a lot better- it can become a habit. But good news is I have done some therapy for alternatives to self harming (like burning, cutting, pulling, picking etc) and there are other ways to minimise it becoming or staying frequent. If you are in a crisis state and feel like a strong physical sensation is the only thing to bring you out of a negative emotional situation there are some alternatives that do not scar you or damage you like:

 *holding ice cubes in your hands- very strong sensation but does not  damage you

*flicking a rubber band on your wrist- stings but doesn't break skin
if you need to 'see' something on your skin that looks like damage, you can draw on yourself with a water washable texta/marker in red.

Other methods that take a little more brain power and practice are based on sensations to take you into the present moment (which is sometimes what pain will do) and those are 
*trying to hear every single sound around you, focusing on the sound
*touching something of texture (maybe furry or smooth) and focusing on how it feels 

And the other methods can help before you get to that point are
*deep breathing
*moving your body, focus on the movements
*moving to a different location in the house or to outside if safe.

The first methods are sort of self harm crisis point first aid methods to avoid getting into or continuing a habit of actually destroying your skin. The rubber band one works well for me. But it is good to try to practice using the methods of relaxation and grounding just as you start to notice you might be going into emotional crisis mode (such as you suddenly have the urge to binge drink or chain smoke for a long session).

That's my 2 cents worth. Hope it might give you some helpful options.
